statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-18447 (PostgreSQL output parameter type confusion executes arbitrary code) affects PostgreSQL 16 releases before 16.16 and is fixed in PostgreSQL 16.16: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-18447/. The PostgreSQL 16.16 release notes list it: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD records it under its 16.16-r0 secfixes entry: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are published at 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64, each built from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version. We unpacked every one of these builds on both architectures. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres in the postgresql16 package, and its version banner in each build matches the package version. 16.16-r0, built from PostgreSQL 16.16, is the first published build carrying the fix. 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 are built from earlier PostgreSQL 16 releases and are affected.

CVE-2026-18447 (PostgreSQL output parameter type confusion executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.12: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-18447/ lists 17.12 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/, include it. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 17.12 and lists CVE-2026-18447 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD at the aports revision for each package version (the current revision is linked above) and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 17 release. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, which ships in the postgresql17 package. The earlier published builds for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0) are built from earlier upstream releases and their server binaries report those older versions, and Alpine applies no backport of this fix to them, so they are recorded as affected; 17.12-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-18447, type confusion in SQL-language functions through an output parameter of type "any" that lets an object creator execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, in 17.12. Within major version 17, releases before 17.12 are affected. https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-18447/, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. Debian fixed it for trixie in postgresql-17 17.12-0+deb13u1 (DSA-6625-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-18447. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
